sections.title: Sound of jota
paragraphs: The name of this letter sounds like (jota) /ˈʒɔtɐ/. It makes the sound /ʒ/, as heard in the word (jogo) /ˈʒo.ɣu/, meaning game. This letter has only one sound in European Portuguese. It is always reliable and never silent. Listen to the smooth buzzing air.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Put your tongue tip near the roof of your mouth, just behind your teeth. Push your lips slightly forward into a round shape. Blow continuous air over your tongue while turning on your vocal cords. You can feel a clear buzz when you place a hand on your throat.

sections.title: Where it appears
paragraphs: This letter always produces the same sound in all positions. You hear the sound /ʒ/ at the start of words like (janela) /ʒɐˈnɛ.lɐ/. It keeps the exact same voice and smooth airflow in every single position. No special accent or nearby vowel changes this rule.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not start this letter with a hard tap like the sound in jam. It never has a stopping sound at the beginning. Do not blow breath from your throat like the Spanish sound either. Say it softly like the middle sound of measure or vision.
